topic: Should our team move to a four-day work week?
briefing: Shared briefing at session start (the thin wiki): the team is deciding whether to adopt a four-day work week. Two concerns dominate — staff wellbeing/output vs. client coverage. Participate independently before seeing others' views.

reads.text: A four-day week boosts wellbeing and focus, and output stays high.
Fewer days improves wellbeing; productivity and focus hold up.
Wellbeing and focus rise with a four-day week; output is maintained.
We need five-day coverage for client response or service suffers.
Client coverage and response times require a five-day week.

steelman_text: The strongest case for the minority: client coverage is a real obligation — if response times slip, the people who depend on the team pay for it. Any move must protect coverage, not wish it away.

evidence.text: Field trials of the four-day week (e.g. the 2022 UK pilot across 61 organisations) report output was maintained when client-facing teams used an explicit coverage rota.
evidence.label: fixture

positions._note: SCENARIO ONLY (decision #9): simulated pre/post stance toward a coverage-aware four-day week, 0..1, with 1..5 confidence. The Habermas data has no evidence dimension, so these are stipulated by the fixture, not data-derived. Uptake is computed from them; it is never presented as data-validated.

rounds.note: round 0 — shallow premature consensus on a platitude, plus the two camp positions
candidates: Whatever we choose, we all want the team to thrive.
Adopt a four-day week to improve wellbeing and focus.
Keep a five-day week to protect client coverage.

rounds.note: round 1 — group drops the platitude; real positions polarise
candidates: Adopt a four-day week; productivity will hold.
Keep five days; client response cannot slip.

rounds.note: round 2 — same positions repeat; no new information (echo begins)
candidates: Adopt a four-day week; productivity will hold.
Keep five days; client response cannot slip.

rounds.note: round 3 — still repeating -> deadlock -> triggers evidence injection
candidates: Adopt a four-day week; productivity will hold.
Keep five days; client response cannot slip.

rounds.note: round 4 — post-injection compromise both camps can endorse -> bridging quorum
candidates: Pilot a four-day week with a Friday on-call rota to keep client coverage.
